topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture, outlines the learning objectives, and sets the framework for understanding cancer evolution and the microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic Clonal Selection and Epigenetic Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through Darwinian selection of genetically mutated clones as well as non-mutational alterations in the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine hierarchical tumor organization and present experimental evidence from leukemia and colorectal cancer regarding whether malignancies originate from stem cells or differentiated progenitors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Promotion of Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters and chronic inflammatory signals cooperate with pre-existing mutations to drive tumor initiation in lung and colorectal tissues.

topics.label: Established Tumor Microenvironments, Spatial Profiling, and Evolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss stromal dependencies in established malignancies, modern spatial profiling methods used to study tumor-microenvironment interactions, and the overarching synthesis of multifactorial cancer coevolution.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Preview of Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and provides logistical framing for the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
